title: What “customizable” means, and how it is tested
gloss: The split between capability (decided by reality, not configurable) and priority (the owner’s, pure configuration) — and the Swap Test, the acceptance test for the whole stage.
body:
The owner's words (OD-51): "when I said change the source of the field from currently one to three, you should just make a small customization change, not a code change." The design (§2.3.5) splits the requirement into two things, and only one of them is configurable:

Capability
Can this source serve this field at all?

Decided by reality, proven by fetching. Not configurable. Nobody may rank BSE first for issue size while BSE is measured 41 to 76 percent low.

Priority
Of the sources that can, which do we prefer?

Decided by the owner. Pure configuration. Swapping rank 1 and 2, or adding a third capable source, never needs a code change or a build.

Acceptance test for the whole stage: the Swap Test. On staging, swap rank 1 and rank 2 of ipos.issue_size (DOC and CHITTORGARH) twice, once through each configuration path, and show at the next wake that (a) the plan row's ranks changed, (b) the walk asked the new rank 1 first, (c) the writer accepted the new rank 1 over the stored value, (d) provenance names the configuration version that produced it, then swap back. If this test cannot be run by the supervisor with zero code edits, stage 3 is not done.

title: The architecture — three layers, one resolver
gloss: Registry, override table and admin protection, all read through one function. The resolver signature and what each component does with it.
body:
Effective priority for a field = the first layer that answers, resolved once per walk and recorded on the plan row and in provenance (§2.3.5). All three layers are read through one function, and every component that needs a rank calls that function and nothing else.

LayerWhat it holdsWho changes itTakes effectLives in
1 Registryscraper/config/field-manifest.json, generated from the spec. Ranks per field per IPO type, capability per source, document type order, unit, N/A offering types, version.A reviewed PR that edits the spec, regenerates the manifest, and ships through the config-only deploy path. Never hand-edited.Next scraper wake after the config deploy (the scraper is a fresh process per wake).git, with a diff, a reviewer, a date and a one-command revert.
2 OverrideTable field_source_overrides: table, field, ipo_id (null = all IPOs), rank1/2/3, reason, set_by, set_at, expires_at (default 30 days).Owner or supervisor through scripts/ops/field-source-override.mjs. Validated before it is stored: every named source must be capable, and E-1 fields may not rank the document.Next wake, no deploy at all.The database, for a same-day change. Expires, so it cannot quietly become the real configuration.
3 AdminThe existing per-IPO, per-field protection row (field_protection_metadata).Admin UI, unchanged.Immediately: the walk skips the field while the row exists, and re-enters it when the row is cleared (§2.7).Already built. Untouched.

The one resolver

// scraper/src/config/field-source-policy.ts   (new; module: config)
resolveFieldSourcePolicy({ table, column, ipoType, ipoId? }) -> {
  ranks: SourceCode[]            // e.g. ['DOC','CHITTORGARH'], ADMIN never listed: it is layer 3
  capable: Record<SourceCode, boolean>
  documentTypeOrder: DocType[]    // what 'DOC' resolves to for this field (OD-30)
  origin: { kind:'registry', version:2 } | { kind:'override', id, expiresAt }
  na: boolean                     // field does not apply to this offering type
}
  • The plan generator writes rank1..3 and manifest_version from the resolver, for every IPO type the manifest resolves.
  • The walk asks sources in ranks order and records origin on the plan row.
  • The writer (data-consolidation-service.ts) decides every conflict from ranks and capable. ADMIN wins first by a fixed invariant, then the ranks. A value from a source not marked capable is refused with the logged reason REJECTED_INCAPABLE_SOURCE and a data_conflicts row, never ranked last.
  • Provenance: every field_sources row written under the policy stores origin in data_lineage, so "why does this field say that?" is answerable after any configuration change.
  • The matrix (field-priority-matrix.ts) keeps only normalization, validation bounds and confidence thresholds. Its sources arrays are deleted. A test asserts none remain.
What stays code, stated plainly (§2.3.5). Reordering sources that already work: configuration. Adding a new source (another website or feed): needs a fetcher and a capability entry proven by fetching, so that is code. Adding a new field: needs a column, an extractor and a check, so that is code.

title: How a change reaches production without a build
gloss: The config-only deploy path: what deploy-config.sh copies, why releases stay immutable, how rollback works.
body:
Today there is no config-only path: every change to scraper/config/ rides a full build on the 2-vCPU box that serves production. The design chose the config-only deploy path over a database-held config (§7.6), because git gives a diff, a reviewer, a date and a revert. Slice S5 builds it:

  1. scripts/ops/deploy-config.sh --slot staging|prod --sha <merged main sha> --reason "..." copies only scraper/config/field-manifest.json from that sha into $ROOT/shared/config/<slot>/ (never into a release: releases stay immutable, review finding 7), verifies the file hash, writes CONFIG_SHA, and appends a log line with who, when, sha and reason. Every release's own scraper/config/field-manifest.json is a symlink to that shared file.
  2. No build, no PM2 restart: the next wake is a fresh process and validates the file at start. The cycle log's manifest-hash line is the proof the new file is live.
  3. Guarded like every deploy: staging any time with the logged reason; prod only on the owner's word. Because it is not a build, the recommendation is to allow a prod config deploy in any evening window, not only the weekly one. This is an owner decision (D-3 below).
  4. Rollback is the same command with the previous sha.

title: The slices, in order
gloss: The original seven slices with the failing test, staging proof and review tier each owes. Read with the corrections below.
body:
One worker at a time. Each slice has a failing test first on the real function, a staging proof read by identity, and its review tier. No slice starts until the previous one's proof is recorded. This table is the original seven; section 8 below splits S1 into S1a to S1d, adds S0c (source-code reconciliation) and S0d (widen the scraper_source enum), and sets the final order. The stage 3 slices section at the top lists every slice as built.

SliceWhat landsFailing test firstStaging proofTier / budget
S0a
spec repair		The spec gets a stated reason on the 37 fields that fell from three sources to two when Moneycontrol was retired; the last Moneycontrol rank is removed; Appendix A and its counts are regenerated; design check D15 is green again.check-design-consistency.mjs --gate is red today on "fewer than three sources with no reason".Gate exit 0; STATS() printed in the PR body.C 15 min / 30 calls
S0b
generate the registry		scripts/generate-field-manifest.mjs writes the manifest from the spec for all 190 sourced fields and the three phase-1 IPO types (§5.5), version 2. scripts/ci/check-field-manifest-current.mjs fails the PR if the committed file differs from the generator, and prints the resolved-plan diff ("these N fields now resolve differently") as the review artifact (§7.6). The loader's schema gains version: 2.The generator must reproduce today's 10 hand-written rows exactly; the CI check must go red on a one-character hand edit.Cycle log prints the new manifest hash at start; 0 loader errors.B 30 min / 60 calls
S1
one resolver, writer adopts it		The resolver above. Writer, walk and generator all call it. Matrix loses its sources. ADMIN-first invariant. Incapable source refused with a logged reason. Provenance stores origin. Rollout per reconciliation group under a config list switchover.groups (OD-44), open and upcoming IPOs first.On the real consolidator: incoming BSE issue size against a stored CHITTORGARH value must be refused as incapable; incoming DOC against stored CHITTORGARH must win; an E-1 field must never accept a document value. Test that no sources: key remains in the matrix.walk-proof.mjs --expect-db ipodhan_staging: at least 3 IPOs MATCH, 0 mismatches, chosen source never BSE for issue size, data_conflicts for issue size in that wake = 0. live test drives the real writer (#732)		The integration suite constructs the real DataConsolidationOrchestrator against ipodhan_test for one WIN and one LOST case; the typed fixture stays for unit tests only.The new suite is red until the walk and the real writer agree end to end.Suite green in CI against ipodhan_test through the tunnel (job log read, not the badge).B 30 min / 60 calls

Then, as the first item after stage 3: the NSE fetcher for the walk, because the timetable, status and subscription fields all start at NSE and today nothing can ask it.

title: Corrections from the independent review
gloss: 2026-09-17, Opus, fresh context. Thirteen findings, each verified against origin/main before acceptance — including a writer whose priority key had no table in it.
body:
Thirteen findings, each verified against origin/main by the supervisor before acceptance. They change the plan as follows; the slice table in section 7 is read together with this section.

#FindingChange to the plan
1The writer has no table in its key. getFieldRules(fieldName) takes a bare camelCase column (field-priority-matrix.ts:906); the two priority calls in the writer (data-consolidation-service.ts:2268) never pass input.tableName. Same column names collide across 18 tables.S1b step 1 becomes: thread tableName and rowKey from the consolidation input into the priority decision, outranksUntrackedValue, isTimeBased and allowsSameSourceRefresh, with its own failing test, before any resolver call.
2Untracked-value rule inverts at two sources. outranksUntrackedValue requires rank < sources.length - 1 (:383-386). Under the manifest issue size has two ranks, so Chittorgarh could no longer replace a value with no provenance, which is exactly how the 27 staging rows and the #728 prod rows must heal.S1b redefines the rule as "ranked and capable may replace an untracked value", with a red test at two-source ranks.
3Source codes the writer cannot store. The spec ranks REG (21 times) and IG (3 times); the manifest schema has REG and the document types but not IG or API_FALLBACK; the writer's ScraperSource has neither DOC nor REG. A price band advertisement write arrives labelled DRHP with its type travelling separately.New S0c: source-code reconciliation. One mapping table from manifest code to writer source plus document-type constraint, covering DOC, REG, IG and API_FALLBACK, reusing mapManifestSourceToScraperSource (field-plan-walk.ts:766) as the single map. Lands before S0b generates 190 rows.
4Deleting every sources array drops live fields to the default order. Grey market premium has a matrix rule but no manifest row and is written by data-persister.ts, which never calls the child-row consolidator.S1d states the fallback contract: a field with no manifest row keeps its matrix sources as a deprecation shim, logged once per cycle. The "no sources: key remains" test moves to S6, after every writable field has a row.
5Two more readers of sources. allowsSameSourceRefresh falls back to rules.sources (:945) and the price-band document-precedence branch depends on it.Named in S1b as must-migrate call sites, each with a red test.
6Dependencies were implied, not stated. S2 writes version 2 rows and cannot run before S0b ships version 2 (schema literal is z.literal(1) today). S5 copies files and depends on nothing.Every card carries explicit edges: S2 needs S0b; S4 needs only S1b's interface; S5 needs nothing and moves early.
7Copying config into current breaks release identity. Releases are immutable checkouts named by sha; the gate cross-checks the served sha (scripts/deploy-linux.sh:17-22, 74). A mutated release lies about its sha and the next deploy silently reverts the config.S5 redesigned: the manifest lives in $ROOT/shared/config/<slot>/, the pattern shared/env and shared/certs already use, symlinked into each release. deploy-config.sh writes the shared file, records the source sha in CONFIG_SHA-<slot>, and the cycle log prints the manifest hash and that sha. Deploys inherit the config.
8IPO type on a create is circular. The writer needs segment and listing exchanges to pick the rank list, and segment is itself a manifest field.S1b rule: on create resolve with MAINBOARD and re-resolve on the next wake; identity fields (segment, listing_exchanges) are exempt from per-type ranking and always use the MAINBOARD list.
9CI can run S3: the PR gate has a scraper integration job on an ephemeral test database with an explicit file list (pr-gate.yml:661-800).S3 Definition of Done adds the literal run-list line; staging-wake proofs stay supervisor-only.
10Missing from the plan: reconciliation groups as a validated config tunable (§7.6), an active-override report distinct from the fail-on-expired check, and the per-cycle re-read statement. Over-built: the resolver need not return capable since the loader already refuses incapable ranks.Reconciliation groups get their own schema and card inside S1b; S6 adds the active-override report; the resolver returns ranks and origin only.
11Reuse the plan missed.S1 imports the existing DOC map; S5 relies on the existing start-time validation; S6's writer check reuses normalizeChosen and areEquivalent.
12Order.New order: S0a → S0b → S0c → S5 → S1a → S1b → S1c → S1d → S2 → S3 → S4 → S6. S5 early gives every later slice a no-build staging turnaround.
13The S2 repair tool's database guard is a name check, not a schema check; prod lacks the plan table until #713 lands.S2 tool asserts the table and the manifest_version column exist and refuses a prod connection unless an explicit flag names that prod has migrated.

Supervisor's own additions from the operations angle: staging does not set ENABLE_FIELD_MANIFEST, so the manifest is validated at start nowhere today; S0b turns it on. The per-slot env file lives under shared/env, which is the precedent S5 now follows. Twelve slices; time estimate unchanged at six to seven working days because S5 early removes a build from every later proof loop.

title: Guardrails that keep configuration from becoming a foot-gun
gloss: Validated at process start, S-05 enforced not remembered, overrides that expire, a rank change reviewed as a diff of the resolved plan.
body:
• Validated at process start, refuse to run on invalid configuration. Schema plus the cross-check that every ranked source is capable. A silently ignored bad rank looks like the change was made (§7.6).
  • S-05 is enforced, not remembered. The ten E-1 timetable fields cannot rank the document, in the registry or in an override. The check is in the loader and in the override tool.
  • A rank change is reviewed as a diff of the resolved plan, never as a JSON diff. The CI check prints it; the PR body must carry it.
  • Overrides expire. Thirty days by default. Permanent changes go to the registry, where they are reviewed.
  • Provenance names the configuration. Registry version or override id on every write.
  • The manifest is never hand-edited. The generator is the only writer; CI refuses drift.
  • Switch-over per reconciliation group (issue size, fresh issue, OFS, price band, lot size move together), proven by two clean staging cycles read by IPO and group, rolled back per field as a config edit (OD-44).
  • Every slice claims its rule ids (R-054, R-055 and the section 7.6 rules) in its card and test header, so the traceability check binds them (OD-52).

title: Rollout and release
gloss: What reaches staging when, what must carry the #713 migrations first, and why existing wrong rows are not hand-repaired.
body:
• Staging: each slice lands on main, deploys in the 13:30 or 21:30 window, is woken by hand, and its proof is read the same hour.
  • Production: nothing here reaches prod before the Saturday 2026-09-19 release. That release must carry the #713 migrations first (prod has no ipo_field_plan table today), then S4's migration if it is ready. The manifest flag stays off on prod until the S1 group proof has held two staging cycles.
  • Existing wrong rows (27 BSE-sourced issue sizes on staging, the #728 class on prod) are not hand-repaired. Once the writer refuses BSE, the walk re-sources them from the document or Chittorgarh; the walk proof tool measures it.

title: The three decisions that are the owner’s
gloss: The slice order (approved 2026-09-17), the 30-day override expiry, and the config-only prod deploy window.
body:
1. D-1 Approve the twelve slices in the section 8 order (S0a, S0b, S0c, S0d, S5, S1a, S1b, S1c, S1d, S2, S3, S4, S6), with the Swap Test as the acceptance test. Approved 2026-09-17.
  2. D-2 Override expiry default: 30 days as the design proposes.
  3. D-3 A production config-only deploy (no build) may run in any evening window, owner-worded, rather than only the weekly release. Recommended: yes, because the cost the weekly rule protects against is the build, and this path has none.

title: Cost, honestly
gloss: Six to seven working days of wall clock, and what the two-day alternative would have left behind.
body: Twelve slices (the seven in section 7, with S1 split into S1a to S1d and S0c/S0d added by the review), one worker at a time, Sonnet builders and Opus reviews on the Tier A slices: about six to seven working days of wall clock, roughly twice the stage 3 in the hand-off. The alternative, wiring the writer to the 10-field manifest, would take two days and leave 180 sourced fields on the old matrix, the walk unable to swap a rank without a build, and a fourth priority table to reconcile later.

title: What changed on 2026-09-18 — prevention replaces repair
gloss: The owner’s redirect, the eight decisions (OD-56 to OD-63) it produced, the witness inventory per segment, and the four CRITICAL findings that killed the first plan.
body:
The owner's redirect: "You are targeting to fix things. What I am targeting is that the issue should not happen at all again... I don't want the scraper to run again and again for the same IPO. First time it should scrape from whatever sources each field has and then compare against each other."

Everything above builds one correct source order. This section is what happens when the scraper runs: every witness a field has is asked in the same pass, their answers are compared immediately, and a verdict is stored beside the value. The failure the old §3 handled after the fact — a wrong value discovered weeks later — is instead caught at the moment of writing.

Why the old model had to go

The measurement that settled it: 14,145 unresolved conflicts across 221 IPOs, the oldest open 96 days, average age 27 days. Susan Electricals' registrar has had two sources disagreeing since 15 June and nothing has ever settled it. The system was good at noticing disagreements and unable to resolve them — a smoke alarm with no fire brigade.

The eight decisions, all merged to the spec tonight

ODDecisionThe measurement behind it
56One pass per stage change (announced → open → closed → listed). Within a stage, a field read successfully is never read again. A field whose source did not exist at the previous stage is a first read, not a re-read.13 UPCOMING IPOs held 5 documents between them — a literal one-scrape-ever rule would publish a blank price band for every IPO filing its RHP after announcement.
57The tie-break varies by field family. Dates and status → the exchange. Money and counts → the document. Names → the document after normalisation. Live numbers → the exchange always. The document is the authority on what the company promised; the exchange on what actually happened.Of 28,946 real disagreements: dates 12,719 (44 IPOs), money 8,938 (229), names 6,344 (55). A global "document always wins" rule would be wrong 12,719 times. Re-measured 2026-09-19 and the 12,719 needs a caveat: all 12,719 are plain YYYY-MM-DD on BOTH sides and 0 are the same date written two ways — they differ by one to four REAL days. So a date COMPARISON fix clears none of them; only the OD-57 tie-break does. Of the 14,141 still unresolved, just 23 dates genuinely differ and 98.4% are OD-60 abstentions.
58Widen the witnesses, at least one outside the offer document — what the exchange publishes, not the document downloaded from it.Re-reading the same PDF proves only that the parser is consistent. 122 of 190 fields already have a non-document witness; zero are document-only-multi.
59Compare meaning, not text. Numbers as numbers, money within 0.5%, identifiers exactly, names after folding corporate forms.Of 28,946 "disagreements", at least 5,384 (19%) were never disagreements: 2,494 same-number-different-text, 1,207 rounding, 1,683 a source returning zero.
60An empty answer is an abstention, not a vote.Refined after measuring: abstention means null/undefined/'' only, never 0 — see the S0 finding below.
61Disagreements are admin-only. No reader ever sees one.Settles a rule that was living in a code comment citing OD-39, which never mentioned disagreements.
62A missing field stores a reason code, never a bare null: SOURCE_UNREACHABLE, NOT_PUBLISHED_YET, EXTRACTION_FAILED, FAILED_VALIDATION.12,701 plan rows across 71 IPOs hold no value, and field_extraction_failures — built for exactly this — holds zero rows.
63/admin/conflicts becomes a data-quality queue — absences listed alongside disagreements, with hand-entry.The dashboard already exists and works: 31,659 of 45,804 conflicts resolved — but every one by SYSTEM. No human has ever used it.

The witness inventory, per segment

The first plan counted witnesses on MAINBOARD only. The independent review caught it: 50 of 190 fields have a different witness count per segment, and two have none at all on one segment.

Witnesses per fieldMAINBOARDSME_BSESME_NSE
0 — no witness by design011
1 — SINGLE_SOURCE688777
2727186
3503126

So the verdict has five states, not four — CONFIRMED, DISPUTED, UNCONFIRMED, SINGLE_SOURCE, NO_WITNESS — and the single-source population is resolved at walk time from the IPO's own segment, never a fixed list. The 68 document-only fields (cin, compliance_officer_phone, cut_off_price) get shape validation and an honest label; calling them "verified" would be a lie.

The slices

SliceWhat it landsTierPRStatus

S9The admin data-quality queue (OD-63)A—queued

What the first plan got wrong, and how it was caught

The implementation plan failed its independent review with four CRITICAL findings, every one reproduced before acceptance. Recording them because the pattern matters more than the fixes:

  • A headline measurement was a tautology. "All 8,010 field instances have one source, so the cross-check never ran" — but field_sources has a unique constraint making one row per field by construction. It would read 8,010/8,010 even if three witnesses voted. The real finding is stronger: the schema cannot record a second witness at all.
  • The flagship proof named an impossible source. It said NSE and the document both answer issue_size; NSE is marked capable: false for that field because it computes issue size excluding the OFS portion. A worker would have fabricated the proof.
  • OD-56 was implemented by no slice — the owner's first and most load-bearing decision. Now S5.
  • The zero rule was backwards. data-consolidation-service.ts already warns: "the emptiness test is === null || === undefined, never falsiness: 0, false and '' are values a source genuinely supplied." The plan said the opposite and would have reversed a deliberate guard on 33 fields where zero is real.

S0's finding killed the problem instead of solving it. All 1,683 zero-conflicts are one field — issueSize — and 1,659 of them (98.6%) came from Moneycontrol, which OD-3 retired. The last was written on 1 September, 17 days ago. So the comparator carve-out for zero is unnecessary: the problem was a source, and the source is already gone. Chittorgarh (21) and BSE (3) account for the rest, both stopped weeks ago.

What this does not do, stated plainly

  • It does not fix the 14,145 existing conflicts. The model prevents new ones; draining the old pile is the admin queue's job (S9).
  • It does not make the single-witness fields trustworthy. Shape validation catches a malformed value, not a wrong one — and no second witness exists to catch a wrong one.
  • It does not add a new external source yet. The four existing witnesses vote first and the gaps get measured; SEBI's filing portal is the named candidate if one is wanted later.

Written 2026-09-17 by the stage 3 supervisor session; section 9 added 2026-09-18 22:40 IST from origin/main 7fc16594. Companion page: the Field Source Ledger, all 240 fields with their approved ranks and the writer's rule today.
